Role Title: English Language Expert (Philippines)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging English Language Experts (Philippines) to contribute to an impactful customer project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.


Scope of Work

  1. Listen to multi-speaker conversational audio recordings, identifying and tagging key speaker and audio metadata such as dialect, accent, audio quality, background noise, age, and speaking style.
  2. Annotate and correct first-pass ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) transcripts, ensuring precise application of Filipino English spelling, usage, and conventions.
  3.   4. Apply your knowledge of Filipino English vocabulary, idioms, slang, code-switching (such as Taglish and Bisaya-English mixing), and spelling to enhance the linguistic accuracy of project data.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Fluent proficiency in Filipino English, with demonstrated familiarity across multiple dialects and regional accents.
  2. Background in language teaching, linguistics, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or a related discipline.
  3. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a meticulous approach to language variation and usage.
  4. Ability to distinguish subtle differences in Filipino English pronunciation and vocabulary across regions and language groups.
  5. Experience working with audio data, metadata tagging, or transcription practices is beneficial.
  6. Adaptable, detail-oriented, and able to manage complex annotation guidelines independently.
  7. Interest in linguistic technology, AI training, or language data projects is a plus.

Job Title: Software Engineer (Staff), Financial Platform & Infra


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


The Role

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to architect and build our financial infrastructure from the ground up. You'll own the systems powering global payouts, payment processing, ledgering, reconciliation, and financial controls, ensuring every expert gets paid accurately and on time.


This is a highly hands-on, high-ownership role for an engineer who has previously designed and built financial systems at scale. You'll set the technical direction for our payments infrastructure, working closely with engineering, finance, operations, and leadership to build reliable systems that can support our next stage of growth.


What You'll Be Doing

  1. Architect and build scalable financial infrastructure from scratch, owning the technical roadmap for global payments and payouts.
  2. Design reliable, idempotent payment workflows across multiple currencies, payment rails, and providers, with safe retries and robust failure handling.
  3. Build double-entry ledgering, reconciliation, and audit systems to ensure accurate tracking of financial transactions.
  4. Integrate global payment providers, banking partners, and payout rails, including ACH, SEPA, SWIFT, and local payment networks.
  5. Develop financial controls, monitoring, approval workflows, and fraud prevention mechanisms to safeguard money movement.
  6. Design resilient, event-driven systems capable of handling provider outages, delayed settlements, failed transactions, and high transaction volumes.
  7. Lead architectural decisions, technical design reviews, and complex migrations while maintaining payment accuracy and operational continuity.
  8. Partner directly with founders, finance, and operations to translate complex financial requirements into reliable, scalable engineering solutions.
  9. Establish engineering best practices for financial correctness, observability, incident response, and long-term platform reliability.


What We're Looking For

  1. 8+ years of backend software engineering experience, including significant technical ownership of production financial systems.
  2. Proven experience architecting and building payment, payout, or ledger infrastructure from scratch, taking systems from initial design through production and scale.
  3. Deep understanding of payment processing, money movement, transaction lifecycles, idempotency, concurrency, and distributed systems.
  4. Hands-on experience designing double-entry ledgers, financial reconciliation processes, and auditable transaction systems.
  5. Experience integrating payment providers and banking infrastructure across multiple payment rails, currencies, and geographies.
  6. Strong backend engineering skills in TypeScript or similar languages, with expertise in SQL, relational databases, and event-driven architectures.
  7. Experience building highly reliable financial systems with robust failure handling, monitoring, security, and operational controls.
  8. Strong understanding of financial data integrity, transaction consistency, and safe migrations of business-critical systems.
  9. Demonstrated ability to independently own complex technical initiatives, make architectural decisions, and deliver production systems in fast-moving environments.
  10. Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with engineering, finance, operations, and executive stakeholders.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Experience building global contractor payouts, payroll infrastructure, or cross-border payment platforms.
  2. Familiarity with financial compliance requirements, including KYC/KYB, sanctions screening, tax documentation, and audit controls.
  3. Experience scaling financial platforms to process millions of dollars monthly across multiple countries.
  4. Familiarity with SOC 2, PCI DSS, or financial audit requirements.
  5. Experience with stablecoin or crypto-based payment infrastructure.
  6. Experience building internal finance tools, reconciliation dashboards, or payment operations platforms.
  7. Experience leveraging AI coding agents and AI-assisted development workflows in production engineering.

  3. Proven ability to debug complex systems, resolve bugs, and deliver effective optimizations.
  4. Experience with large codebase refactoring and legacy system modernization.
  5. Track record of delivering high-impact features from conception through delivery.
  6. Strong documentation and communication skills to articulate technical concepts clearly.
  7. Interest in AI and its technical challenges — previous AI experience not required.

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required may vary depending on your experience and workflow.

Job Title: Competitive Coder

Job Type: Contractor (15hrs+ a week)

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $30 - $100

Commitment: 15+ hours per week

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Strong competitive programming background and advanced C++

Your tasks: Create original competitive programming problems with reference solutions and robust test suites


You’ll create Reinforcement Learning Environments that test a model’s ability to solve hard algorithmic problems. Each task means writing an original problem that doesn’t exist on any online judge, a correct reference solution, and a test suite strong enough that a wrong solution fails.


What you’ll do

  1. Design original competitive programming problems, absent from Codeforces, AtCoder, and all other judges.
  2. Write a correct reference solution and verify it against the constraints.
  3. Build a robust test suite: edge cases, maximum constraints, and tests that break plausible wrong approaches.
  4. Implement checkers for problems with multiple valid outputs.
  5. Document the problem’s intended solution, complexity, and the reasoning behind your test cases.
  6. Review problems from other contributors for correctness and test coverage.
  7. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or have unintended solutions.

What we’re looking for

  1. Strong competitive programming record — Codeforces, AtCoder, ICPC, IOI, or equivalent.
  2. Advanced C++ for reference solutions and checkers.
  3. Deep algorithmic knowledge and the ability to reason about constraints, complexity, and edge cases.
  4. Meticulous attention to detail in validation and output consistency.
  5. Clear written and verbal English for documenting problems and edge cases.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines.
  7. Prior experience as a problem setter, tester, or checker on a major platform is a strong plus.


Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required may vary depending on your experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

次世代のパーソナルロボットのトレーニングにご協力ください。UMIグリッパー（ロボットの手を模倣しながら、自然な動作で作業を行えるウェアラブルデバイス）を使用して、日常的な家事作業の高品質な動画デモンストレーションを撮影していただきます。あなたのデモンストレーションは、ロボットが実際の家庭で作業する方法を学ぶためのトレーニングデータとなります。

  1. UMIグリッパー（ウェアラブルデバイス）を使用し、日常的な家事作業について、仕様に準拠した高品質な動画デモンストレーションを撮影・提出する。

  5. クライアントのプロジェクトチームと、文章・口頭の両方で、積極的かつ明確にコミュニケーションを取る。

  6. 設備の整った日本の住環境（キッチン、居住スペース、一般的な生活用品）を常時利用できること。

  8. 本業務ではVRヘッドセットを長時間使用します。通常の業務の一環として、長時間の装着に抵抗がない方が対象です。


歓迎スキル・経験

  1. パーソナルロボット、AI、家庭における新しいテクノロジーへの純粋な好奇心。
  2. データ収集、ユーザビリティ調査、または類似の実践的なプロジェクトへの参加経験。
  3. 反復的で精度を求められる作業への忍耐力と、プロジェクトのニーズの変化に柔軟に対応する姿勢。

標準レート時給12からスタートし、作業効率が上がるにつれて、実質時給を最大21まで引き上げることが可能です。

開始時期・稼働について

通常48時間以内に採用が決定するため、すぐに業務を開始できる方を求めています。選考を通過された場合、応募手続きを進め次第、最初のタスクに着手していただけると幸いです。オンボーディング完了後、約24時間以内にタスクを開始していただくことを想定しています。


機材要件

本プロジェクトでは、VRヘッドセットと、手の動きおよび作業の映像を記録するウェアラブルハンドトラッキンググローブ一式を装着した状態で家事作業を行っていただきます。すべての機材は無料でお届けし、オンボーディング時にセットアップと使用方法について詳しくご案内します。オンボーディングで説明されるスペース、照明、通信環境の要件をご自宅が満たしていることをご確認ください。

Role Title: Finance Research Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $30 - $60 per hour

Time per task: around 4 to 8 hours

Location: Remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Hands-on experience reading US SEC filings and familiarity with US GAAP

Your tasks: Write finance research questions with a verified, sourced answer, and check each one against what AI models answer


Scope of Work

You will work on questions about real US public companies. Each question points to information that sits in long filings or IR materials, or that requires comparing several of them to find the right answer.


  1. Write questions that require finding a specific figure in a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statement, earnings release or investor presentation.
  2. Write questions where two documents show different numbers and the answer depends on knowing which one is correct (for example, original vs. restated figures, or adjusted vs. reported).
  3. Pay attention to period and document version: the right fiscal year, the right filing, the latest amended version.
  4. Test each question against current AI models and keep only the ones they answer incorrectly.

You should also be comfortable reading long filings, including footnotes and tables, and have clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.

Role Title: Music & Sound Annotation Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Music & Sound Annotation Experts to contribute to a customer's project at the forefront of music and audio technology.

Your ears are the ground truth. You'll listen to short field recordings and document exactly what's audible — instruments, tempo, key, background sounds, crowd reactions — through a structured web platform built for this project. Later phases involve grading AI model answers against what you actually heard.


What you'll do

  1. Listen to 30–90 second field recordings (headphones, your own quiet workspace) and complete structured annotations: which instruments are present, tempo and key, timestamps of background events (traffic, sirens, applause), scene details
  2. Compare paired recordings of the same song captured at different locations and judge what stayed the same and what changed
  3. In later phases: review AI model descriptions of clips and mark what's correct, wrong, or invented, with a brief written explanation
  4. Attend a paid onboarding/calibration session and a short weekly sync


Who we're looking for (any of these backgrounds)

  1. Working or gigging musicians, session players, producers, or mixing engineers
  2. Music educators, ear-training instructors, band/choir directors, conservatory students or graduates
  3. Location sound recordists, sound designers, foley artists, or podcast/documentary audio editors


Requirements

  1. 3+ years of hands-on music or audio experience
  2. Strong analytical listening: you can pick individual instruments out of a busy, noisy, real-world mix — not just studio recordings
  3. Can identify tempo (within a few BPM) and musical key (relative pitch with a reference is fine)
  4. Comfortable with detail-oriented, repetitive annotation work in a web platform — dropdowns, timestamps, short structured notes
  5. Clear written English for brief, evidence-based notes (e.g., "accordion enters around 0:12")
  6. Quality headphones, quiet workspace, reliable internet
  7. Available 20–25 hrs/week for the engagement window

Role Title: Principal Engineer / Professor — Technical Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in an engineering or physical science field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


micro1 is engaging principal-level engineers, scientists, and faculty to design the technical problems that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain expertise is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


We’re building this across four areas: aerospace, semiconductors, manufacturing and industrial engineering, and materials science. If your work sits in one of those — or across two of them — this is for you.


The work draws on what you already know: the problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong.


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area, with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in engineering, physics, materials, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major engineering organization, a national lab, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one area, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another expert could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Job Title: Member of Technical Staff, Model Training (post-training research)


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


The Role

In this role, you will investigate how learning algorithms, training data, and evaluation methodologies interact to produce stronger reasoning, generalization, and agent capabilities. You will explore new approaches to reinforcement learning, distillation, and data-efficient training, translating research insights into scalable methods that improve model intelligence.


This is a highly experimental role at the intersection of fundamental machine learning research and large-scale model development. You will have the opportunity to formulate research hypotheses, design ambitious experiments, and develop training methods that directly influence the capabilities of our models.


What You'll Do

  1. Research, implement, and scale advanced post-training methods, including supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning (RL), and on-policy distillation (OPD), across large language and multimodal models.
  2. Investigate learning objectives, optimization dynamics, exploration strategies, and credit assignment mechanisms to improve training stability, sample efficiency, and capability acquisition.
  3. Develop and refine training recipes by jointly optimizing data mixtures, sampling strategies, curricula, and evaluation methodologies.
  4. Design methods for learning from expert demonstrations, human preferences, corrections, and model-generated trajectories, identifying where human feedback delivers the greatest improvements.
  5. Research the co-evolution of generators, reward models, and graders, developing approaches that improve both model performance and the quality of the training signals they consume.
  6. Design rigorous experiments, ablation studies, and evaluation frameworks to measure generalization, reasoning, and performance on realistic downstream tasks.
  7. Own research initiatives end-to-end, from identifying promising directions and implementing new algorithms to executing large-scale experiments and validating results.


What We're Looking For

  1. Strong foundations in machine learning, deep learning, optimization, and modern model training techniques.
  2. Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or post-training large-scale language or multimodal models.
  3. Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as reinforcement learning, model distillation, reward modeling, data selection, or learning dynamics.
  4. Strong proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with the ability to implement, debug, and optimize complex training pipelines.
  5. Experience designing controlled experiments, interpreting model behavior, and translating empirical findings into actionable research directions.
  6. Ability to independently navigate ambiguous research problems, formulate hypotheses, and iterate quickly based on experimental evidence.
  7. Strong analytical thinking and a research-driven mindset, with an emphasis on reproducibility, scientific rigor, and measurable improvements.

Job Title: Member of Technical Staff, Data Engineering


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


The Role

This is a Staff-level, hands-on engineering role for someone who has built data infrastructure from zero to production and knows how to turn fragmented operational data into reliable, accessible, and actionable systems.


You'll own the architecture and implementation of our data warehouse, ingestion pipelines, transformations, and product analytics foundations.


We're building an AI-native organization where both humans and autonomous agents need access to trustworthy, well-structured data. You'll design the systems that make this possible, enabling self-service analytics, automated decision-making, and increasingly intelligent workflows across the company.


What You'll Do

  1. Build our data platform from zero: Architect and implement our internal data warehouse, ingestion infrastructure, ETL/ELT pipelines, and core data models.
  2. Create agent-ready data foundations: Design reliable, well-documented datasets and interfaces that AI agents can safely discover, query, and use.
  3. Turn messy data into trusted systems: Transform fragmented operational and product data into consistent, high-quality sources of truth.
  4. Enable self-service analytics: Build the infrastructure that allows engineering, product, and business teams to answer questions independently without relying on manual data requests.
  5. Own product analytics infrastructure: Establish the event tracking, instrumentation, data models, and reporting foundations needed to understand product usage and performance.
  6. Automate data operations: Leverage AI coding agents and intelligent automation to accelerate pipeline development, data validation, documentation, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
  7. Build for reliability and scale: Establish data quality standards, observability, governance, and scalable architectural patterns from the beginning.
  8. Raise the engineering bar: Mentor engineers, establish strong data engineering practices, and lead architectural decisions through hands-on execution.


What We're Looking For

  1. Staff-level engineering expertise with extensive hands-on experience building and operating production data platforms.
  2. Proven greenfield experience: You've personally led the design and implementation of a data platform from scratch, rather than exclusively maintaining or extending existing infrastructure.

descriptions.14883aba-fc23-4ca4-8935-9d8d72794668:
Role Title: Small/Medium Business – Robotics Data Collection Partner


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is looking for small to medium business owners who want to participate in a paid video data collection project for AI.


Your business would help collect real videos of normal work happening in your workplace. These videos will help train AI systems to better understand how people complete real-world tasks.


You do not need experience with AI. We are looking for business owners with active teams and real day-to-day work.


Who can participate

Your business may be a good fit if you:

  1. Are an owner, partner, or co-owner of a business in LATAM, the United States, or Canada
  2. Have at least 2 employees who can participate
  3. Have regular work activities that can be recorded safely
  4. Can have each participating employee record at least 10 hours of work
  5. Can get permission to record in the workplace
  6. Can make sure participating employees agree to be recorded
  7. Can start soon after a short onboarding call
  8. Employees will use their own iPhone or Android phone to record. Their phone must have an ultra-wide camera and the required motion sensors.


Businesses that may be a good fit

Examples include:

  1. Construction, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, painting, and renovation businesses
  2. Auto repair, equipment repair, and maintenance businesses
  3. Machine shops, fabrication shops, woodworking, and manufacturing businesses
  4. Warehouses, logistics, delivery, and fulfillment businesses
  5. Landscaping, cleaning, pest control, and property maintenance businesses
  6. Catering companies, bakeries, restaurants, and commercial kitchens
  7. Hardware stores, garden centers, greenhouses, and nurseries
  8. The best fit is a business where employees do different hands-on tasks throughout the day. Assembly-line or highly repetitive work is not a fit.


Privacy and consent

We take privacy seriously. Before recording starts, the business owner must make sure employees agree to participate and that the business has permission to record.

Participants should not record any sensitive information.


Payment

Businesses are paid based on the amount and quality of approved video data collected.


Requirements

  1. You own or help run a business in LATAM, the United States, or Canada
  2. You have at least 2 employees who can participate
  3. Each employee can record at least 10 hours weekly
